subject: Post-call: capacity comparison & dedicated pilot plan

Subject: Thanks for the call — next on capacity comps

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the intro call earlier today — Daniel and I appreciated the clear framing. We wanted to capture the asks so we can move toward a side-by-side evaluation:

- Primary goal: replacement of our current inference stack (hyperscaler-managed GPUs) for customer-facing chat with tighter latency controls and lower 95/99p cost.
- Key tests we need: p99 latency at target concurrency, cold-start behavior, throughput under steady-state, and failover/region bump tests.
- Compliance: SOC2 would be a hard req for production; in pilot we can do limited PII-free traffic.
- Rough scale: peak ~250 concurrent requests, avg payload ~300 tokens, occasional 1k-token long-tail.

Could you send a short proposal that compares dedicated reserved capacity vs our existing reserved instances on the hyperscaler? Specifically we want: pricing ballpark, what guarantees you can provide (SLA/latency/capacity), and an outline for a 2-week pilot we can run.

Thanks — Emma

Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next on capacity comps

Hi Emma — great to speak with you and Daniel. Quick recap + proposed next steps below. Attaching a concise capacity matrix and a starter SOW for the pilot.

Recap of objectives (we heard):
- Deterministic p99 latency under 250 concurrent users; handle 1k-token tails gracefully.
- Lower unit cost at 95p/99p compared to hyperscaler reservations when optimized.
- Maintain enterprise controls (SOC2, customer data separation) during pilot.

Why Redwood Dedicated vs hyperscaler reserved instances (short):
- Serving runtime tuned for LLM inference: continuous batching, KV cache/prefix caching, and low-overhead kernel selection — gives lower p99 for the same GPU footprint.
- Capacity guarantees: Dedicated pools are customer-isolated GPU pools with an SLA on throughput and failover policies; hyperscaler reserved instances still compete for noisy neighbors on shared inference layers and can show more variance.
- Predictable economics: we provide tooling (Optimize) that recommends batching/quantization profiles to hit target unit costs; hyperscaler RIs typically lack model-aware batching optimizations out of the box.
- Operational fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallback and cross-region routing if a pool is constrained — keeps user-facing features online.

Proposed 2-week pilot plan (high level):
1) Day 0–1: baseline smoke tests from your existing infra to establish p50/p95/p99 and token-cost baseline.
2) Day 2–5: deploy a 3-node dedicated pool (similar instance types to your current GPUs), run steady-state throughput and cold-start scenarios, collect traces.
3) Day 6–10: enable KV/prefix cache and tuned batching; run long-tail 1k-token tests and failure-injection (simulated node loss + failover).
4) Day 11–14: cost/latency comparison report + recommended commit size for production.

Questions for you to finalize pilot sizing:
- Can you share representative request traces (anonymized) or a sample of token-length distribution?
- Are there any regions beyond us-west that matter for failover testing?

Next steps:
- Ill schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive with Marissa to lock test matrix if that works.
- Attached: capacity_matrix.xlsx (suggested node counts & expected p99 per profile), SOW-draft.pdf.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

- Compliance: we need SOC2 for production; pilot traffic will be scrubbed and PII removed.

Please include a short pricing sketch so the procurement folks can triage. Wed like the pilot to start next Monday if possible.

—Emma
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Pricing sketch & reserved vs dedicated notes

Emma — thanks for the quick responses. High-level pricing options (ballpark; final will depend on selected GPU class and realized token mix):
- Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit): $22k/mo for a 3-node pool sized for your 250 concurrent target (includes reserved capacity and 99.9% uptime objective). Commit options at 6/12 months available for 10–20% discounts.
- Short pilot (2-week dedicated trial): we can provision the 3-node pool for a capped trial fee of $1,500 plus usage overage if you request full production traffic. This includes monitoring, test support, and a pilot technical report.
- Hyperscaler equivalent (est): your current reserved instances at a hyperscaler (no Redwood layer) typically cost similar raw GPU-hours but often require additional engineering to achieve our serving-level p99s — hidden ops cost and variable latency.

Key contractual differentiators:
- Capacity SLA: dedicated pools have explicit throughput and policy-backed fallback clauses; hyperscaler RIs rarely include application-level p99 guarantees without managed inference add-ons.
- Data isolation: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and optional private control plane for audit logs (helpful for SOC2).

Pilot checklist (what wed need ASAP):
- Anonymized traces (upload link or s3).
- Contact for procurement to set a purchase order for the capped trial fee.
- Preferred start date (you mentioned next Monday).

Ive added a HubSpot quick link in the attached related_links for tracking. Marissa will run the deep technical tests and collate telemetry.

—Rishi
